## Subtracting a bracket {#subtract-bracket}

In $-2(x+3)$, the multiplier is **$-2$**. Multiply both terms inside the bracket by $-2$.

:::::: {.example-pair}
::::: {.model}

<h3>Worked example</h3>

$5x-2(x+3)=x+10$

::: {.fragment}

[Multiply both terms by $-2$.]{.annotation}

$5x-2x-6=x+10$

:::
::: {.fragment}

[Collect like terms on the left.]{.annotation}

$3x-6=x+10$

:::
::: {.fragment}

[Subtract $x$ from both sides.]{.annotation}

$2x-6=10$

:::
::: {.fragment}

[Add $6$ to both sides.]{.annotation}

$2x=16$

:::
::: {.fragment}

[Divide both sides by $2$.]{.annotation}

$\dfrac{2x}{2}=\dfrac{16}{2}\quad\Rightarrow\quad x=8$

:::
:::::
::::: {.paper}
::: {.fragment}

<h3>Your turn</h3>

$5x-2(x-3)=x+10$

Only the sign inside the bracket changes. Predict the sign of the expanded constant, then solve.

:::
::: {.fragment}

[Check your working]{.annotation}

$\begin{aligned}
5x-2x+6&=x+10\\
3x+6&=x+10\\
2x+6&=10\\
2x&=4\\
x&=2
\end{aligned}$

Here $(-2)(-3)=+6$. Keep that sign when simplifying.

:::
